ads_ratio.reason: Pembina is a direct-listed foreign private issuer: one NYSE-traded PBA share is one common share, so no ADS conversion applies; per-share figures and the traded price are on the same basis.
ads_ratio.source: Form 40-F / company disclosure: Pembina's common shares trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange (PPL) and the New York Stock Exchange (PBA) — the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS; the _system README v5.3 note likewise lists PBA among the direct-listed ordinary-share filers (ratio 1.0)

moat_against: Larger rivals Enbridge and TC Energy compete for the same Western Canadian volumes and growth projects
Marketing & New Ventures retains commodity-margin exposure — not all earnings are fee-based
New pipeline/facility growth needs Canadian regulatory approvals and producer volume growth; long-term hydrocarbon demand is in structural decline
Levered balance sheet: net debt 5.4x normalized OE (engine) constrains flexibility if volumes or margins fall
Share count is rising (~1.7%/yr engine share CAGR), diluting per-share growth
moat_for: Irreplaceable integrated midstream network in Western Canada — pipelines, gathering/processing, fractionation and export terminals that cannot be replicated on an investable timeline
Predominantly fee-based, long-term contracted toll-road cash flows — producers pay for capacity, insulating the core from direct commodity prices
Leading NGL franchise: Redwater fractionation (RFS IV added 55,000 bpd in May 2026) and Montney/Duvernay basin position
Strategic corridors and export optionality: Alliance (rich gas to Chicago), Cochin, Cedar LNG and LPG export terminals diversify end markets beyond the US
Proven through-cycle OE: owner's earnings positive in 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (engine), including the 2020 downturn
moat_justification: Irreplaceable Western Canadian midstream infrastructure with predominantly fee-based, long-term contracted cash flows, a leading NGL/fractionation franchise at Redwater, and strategic export corridors (Alliance, Cedar LNG) — a strong 7/10. It is not a 9-10: Enbridge/TC Energy are larger rivals, Marketing & New Ventures keeps commodity exposure, growth depends on regulatory approvals and producer volumes, and long-term hydrocarbon demand declines.
name: PEMBINA PIPELINE CORPORATION
one_liner: Strong fee-based midstream franchise, moat 7/10 — but at $48.52 the price is nearly double the 15%-hurdle value: weighted IRR 9.1%, weighted IV@15 $25.11; clears 15% only below ~$25.11.
